scope: India: central-government auction of hydrocarbon exploration acreage - NELP, HELP/OALP, DSF and Special CBM rounds - plus the KG-D6 audit and arbitration record
readThisFirst: This file's central statistic is the share of auctioned blocks that drew exactly one bid. That share is 3.64 per cent in OALP Round I (2018) and 79.49 per cent across Rounds VI, VII and VIII (2021-2023), measured from DGH's own block-by-block bid tables in both cases. Those are the only four OALP rounds for which such a table exists; 78 of the 172 awarded blocks have no published bid count at all. Nothing in this file establishes a single-bidder rate for the NELP era, because no NELP round has a published bid count.

regimes.name: New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP)
regimes.fiscalModel: Production sharing contract. Government and contractor share PROFIT petroleum after the contractor recovers cost, with the split geared to an investment multiple. This is the model that requires the state to audit the contractor's costs.

NELP was approved by the Union Cabinet in 1997 and the first round was launched in 1999; the 1997 Cabinet decision was NOT retrieved for this file, so the regime start is dated to the first round launch that DGH prints, not to the Cabinet approval.

regimes.name: Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP), implemented through the Open Acreage Licensing Programme (OALP)
regimes.fiscalModel: REVENUE sharing contract. The government takes a share of gross revenue from sale and does not audit the contractor's costs. This is the decisive change from NELP: cost recovery and the investment multiple are abolished.
srcs: PIB / Cabinet - Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) approved by the Union Cabinet, 10 March 2016
https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/printrelease.aspx?relid=137638
PIB / MoPNG - India's OALP maiden Bid Round takes off spectacularly: 110 bids received for 55 exploration blocks, 2 May 2018
https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=179079&reg=3&lang=2
features: uniform licence for conventional and unconventional hydrocarbons under one contract
open acreage - bidders carve out their own blocks from a designated area using National Data Repository data and submit Expressions of Interest year-round
easy-to-administer revenue sharing model replacing profit sharing based on investment multiple and cost recovery
marketing and pricing freedom for crude oil and natural gas produced
graded royalty falling from shallow water to deepwater to ultra-deepwater; onland royalty unchanged; no cess and no import duty on blocks awarded under the policy
regimes.notes: The Cabinet decision is dated 10 March 2016 in the PIB release; PIB's own later releases variously describe HELP as 'promulgated on 30 March 2016' and as 'approved in March 2016'. The 10 March date is the Cabinet approval as announced; the 30 March date used in DGH-facing releases is not reconciled in any document opened for this file, and both are recorded rather than one being silently chosen.

regimes.name: February 2019 reform of HELP: shift from revenue maximisation to production maximisation
srcs: PIB / MoPNG - MoPNG launches OALP Bid Round-VI, 6 August 2021
https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1743116
PIB / MoPNG - Contracts for 7 blocks awarded under OALP Bid Round-IV, 2 January 2020
https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1598294&reg=3&lang=2
regimes.notes: PIB records that after three OALP rounds the government notified further policy reforms in February 2019 which shifted the focus from 'revenue' to 'production' maximisation, gave higher weight to the work programme in Category-I basins, and REMOVED revenue share from the bidding parameters entirely for Category-II and Category-III basins. Rounds IV onward were run under this reformed policy. This matters for any competition analysis: from Round IV the bid parameter in Category II and III basins is work programme alone, so 'price' is not what is being competed for. The exact gazette or ministry notification of February 2019 was not retrieved; the date is as stated in two PIB releases.

rounds.notes: TIER IS 'reported', NOT 'documented', for the bid figures: DGH published no Part-I bid table for this round. PSU Watch reports 35 private-sector bids and 28 PSU bids - 63 in total - for 28 blocks, with ONGC bidding on 19 (14 alone, 4 with OIL and IOC, 1 with Reliance and BP), Oil India on 9, Vedanta on ALL 28 and Sun Petrochemicals on 7, and states that every block drew a minimum of two and a maximum of three bids. If that is right the single-bid count is zero. THE MECHANISM MATTERS MORE THAN THE NUMBER: the zero is produced by one company bidding on every single block on offer, so 'no block received a single bid' and 'competition on most blocks was one state company against one private company' are the same fact. The award outcome (28 blocks, 1,36,596 sq km, RSCs signed 15 April 2025, 38 per cent of the area in formerly No-Go zones) IS documented from PIB and the DGH awardee list.

kgD6.claim: The KG-DWN-98/3 (KG-D6) deepwater block, 7,645 sq km, was awarded in the FIRST NELP round in 2000 to a consortium of Reliance Industries Limited (operator) and Niko Resources Limited with 90:10 participating interests. The production sharing contract was signed in April 2000.
srcs: CAG Report No. 19 of 2011 - Performance Audit of Hydrocarbon Production Sharing Contracts, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Chapter 4: Findings relating to KG-DWN-98/3 block (scanned PDF; pages read as page images because the file carries no text layer)
https://cag.gov.in/uploads/download_audit_report/2011/Union_Performance_Civil_Hydrocarbon_Production_Sharing_Contracts_Ministry_of_Petroleum_19_2011_chapter_4.pdf
kgD6.notes: Verbatim from paragraph 4.1 of CAG Report No. 19 of 2011. Water depth 400 m in the north-west to 2,700 m in the south-east. 19 discoveries were made in the block between 2002 and 2008, 18 gas and one oil.

kgD6.claim: The approved capital expenditure for the D1-D3 development rose from US$ 2.39 billion in the Initial Development Plan of May 2004 to US$ 8.8 billion in the Addendum approved in December 2006.

https://cag.gov.in/uploads/download_audit_report/2011/Union_Performance_Civil_Hydrocarbon_Production_Sharing_Contracts_Ministry_of_Petroleum_19_2011_chapter_4.pdf
kgD6.notes: CAG paragraph 4.1, verbatim chain: the IDP of May 2004 was for 40 mmscmd from probable reserves of 5.3 tcf with 34 producing wells and capex of US$ 2.39 billion, approved by the Management Committee on 5 November 2004. In October 2006 RIL submitted an Addendum for 80 mmscmd with probable reserves of 11.3 tcf and Phase-I capex of US$ 5.2 billion with 22 producing wells; in November 2006, after technical exchanges with DGH, it revised this to Phase-I US$ 5.2 billion plus Phase-II US$ 3.6 billion, US$ 8.8 billion in total with 50 producing wells, approved by the Management Committee on 12 December 2006. A SEPARATE plan for the D-26 (MA) oil field with capex of US$ 2.23 billion was submitted in August 2007 and approved in April 2008. THE ESCALATION IS A DOCUMENTED FACT ABOUT APPROVED BUDGETS. It is not, in this record, a finding that the costs were inflated: the capacity target doubled from 40 to 80 mmscmd and the producing-well count rose from 34 to 50 over the same revision, and the CAG report itself carries a highlighted box stating 'We appreciate the efforts of the operator in executing this world class mega greenfield deepwater oil and gas infrastructure in India within record time.'

kgD6.claim: CAG found that, contrary to the PSC, the contractor was allowed to enter the second and third exploration phases without relinquishing 25 per cent of the contract area at the end of each of Phase-I and Phase-II, and that in February 2009 the Government approved treating the ENTIRE 7,645 sq km contract area as 'discovery area', which removed any obligation to relinquish acreage at all.
srcs: CAG Report No. 19 of 2011 - Performance Audit of Hydrocarbon Production Sharing Contracts, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Chapter 4: Findings relating to KG-DWN-98/3 block (scanned PDF; pages read as page images because the file carries no text layer)
https://cag.gov.in/uploads/download_audit_report/2011/Union_Performance_Civil_Hydrocarbon_Production_Sharing_Contracts_Ministry_of_Petroleum_19_2011_chapter_4.pdf
kgD6.notes: CAG paragraph 4.2.1, headed 'Acceptance by DGH and MoPNG of entire contract area of KG-DWN-98/3 as discovery area not in terms of the PSC'. Articles 4.1 and 4.2 of the PSC provide for phased relinquishment down to 75 per cent and then 50 per cent of the contract area, with only discovery and development areas retained at the end of the exploration period. This is the audit finding that goes to the ADMINISTRATION of the contract, and it is directed at DGH and the ministry as much as at the operator.

kgD6.claim: CAG recorded that it was given incomplete access to the operator's accounting system and could NOT quantify the effect of the accounting treatments it questioned.
srcs: CAG Report No. 19 of 2011 - Performance Audit of Hydrocarbon Production Sharing Contracts, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Chapter 4: Findings relating to KG-DWN-98/3 block (scanned PDF; pages read as page images because the file carries no text layer)
https://cag.gov.in/uploads/download_audit_report/2011/Union_Performance_Civil_Hydrocarbon_Production_Sharing_Contracts_Ministry_of_Petroleum_19_2011_chapter_4.pdf
kgD6.notes: THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE FACT FOR READING THE KG-D6 AUDIT AND IT IS THE ONE MOST OFTEN LEFT OUT. CAG records that the operator declined full SAP access on the ground that the E&P Division sits inside the RIL group and the system could not be restricted to KG-DWN-98/3; that a proposed database restore was later abandoned as not feasible; that the Excel line-item extract supplied instead contained only the debit side of transactions and did not reconcile with the trial balance; and that 222 of 337 purchase orders over US$ 1 million did not appear in the data supplied. On the inventory valuation point CAG states in terms: 'due to limited data/details as well as very restricted SAP access, we were not able to quantify the impact of adopting Weighted Average method of valuation as against FIFO method'. MoPNG replied (July 2011) that SAP could give auditors selective read access and that the operator would be instructed through the Management Committee to reconfigure the system. CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY CLAIM BUILT ON THIS REPORT: the CAG did not publish a rupee or dollar loss figure for KG-D6. Anyone citing a KG-D6 'loss' number is citing something other than this audit report.

kgD6.claim: CAG Report No. 19 of 2011 contains no presumptive-loss or notional-loss estimate for the KG-D6 block comparable to the figures published in the 2G report.

kgD6.notes: RECORDED AS A DOCUMENTED ABSENCE under this project's absence rule. Established by reading Chapter 4 of the report - the chapter devoted entirely to KG-DWN-98/3 - which reports findings on relinquishment, development-plan approval, procurement and audit access, and which expressly states that audit could not quantify the impact of the accounting treatment it questioned. LIMIT OF THIS CHECK: Chapter 4 of the report is a scanned image with no text layer, so it could not be keyword-searched; it was read page by page as images, and the pages read were the chapter opening, the relinquishment finding and the closing audit-access pages. A quantified figure elsewhere in the 8-chapter report cannot be excluded on the strength of that reading. Treat this as 'no loss figure found in the KG-D6 chapter', not as 'the report contains no figure anywhere'.

The sum in issue is reported at over US$ 1.729 billion. THE UNDERLYING JUDGMENT PDF WAS NOT OPENED for this file; the neutral citation, date, bench and holdings come from a legal publisher's report of it. baseRates.reading: DISCRIMINATING. Four fifths of blocks in these three rounds drew a single bid. Round VI: 18 of 21 (85.71 per cent), and ONGC was the only bidder on 16 of them. Round VII: 6 of 8 (75 per cent). Round VIII: 7 of 10 (70 per cent). Three bidders participated in Round VI, four in Round VII, five bidding entities in Round VIII. INNOCENT READING, which must ship with this: under the February 2019 reform the bid parameter in Category-II and Category-III basins is the work programme alone, with no revenue-share component, and the blocks are self-carved by bidders from their own Expressions of Interest. A block carved out by one company to suit its own acreage position is, by design, unlikely to attract a rival bid; a single bid on a self-nominated block is what open acreage produces when demand is thin, and is not by itself evidence of anything having been arranged. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the identity of the EoI originator for each block. If the sole bidder is systematically the company whose EoI created the block, the single-bid rate is a mechanical property of open acreage. If it is systematically someone else, that is a different and much more interesting fact. DGH does not publish EoI originators, and that is the single most valuable missing field in this file.

gaps: BIDS RECEIVED PER ROUND IS THE CENTRAL HOLE. DGH published a block-by-block bid table for four OALP rounds only - I, VI, VII and VIII. Rounds II, III, IV, V, IX and X have no such table in any source opened for this file, so 94 of the 172 awarded blocks carry a bid count and 78 do not. Every single-bidder figure in this file is computed against 94 or against a named subset of it, never against 172.

OALP Round-IX bid counts are 'reported', not 'documented'. The 63-bid total, the per-company bid counts and the statement that no block drew a single bid come from PSU Watch's report of 25 September 2024. DGH's own Part-I bid opening summary for Round IX was searched for on dghindia.gov.in and in the Internet Archive's index of that domain and was not found.

OALP Round-X is unresolved. Bidding had been extended four times as at February 2026 and no bid or award data exists. The two ministry figures for the acreage offered - 1,91,986.21 sq km in the August 2025 Rajya Sabha reply and 1,82,589.21 sq km in the April 2025 ministerial statement - are not reconciled by any document opened here.

NO NELP ROUND HAS A BID COUNT. DGH's 2011-12 annual report tabulates blocks offered, awarded, relinquished and operational for all nine NELP rounds but not bids received. Only NELP-VII carries a partial figure - bids were received for 44 of 57 offered blocks. Without bid counts, no single-bidder share can be computed for the entire 1999-2010 production-sharing era, so this file CANNOT answer whether single-bidding got worse after the 2016 regime change. It can only show what happened within the OALP era.

The identity of the Expression-of-Interest originator for each OALP block is not published. Under open acreage, bidders carve out their own blocks and submit EoIs, and DGH then puts the resulting block to competitive bid. Whether the sole bidder on a single-bid block is the company that nominated it is the fact that decides whether a high single-bid rate is a mechanical artefact of the design or something else. It is missing for every one of the 172 blocks.

Block-level work-programme commitments are not published for any OALP block. Round totals exist for some rounds (about Rs 6,000 crore for Round I, Rs 465 crore of immediate commitment for Round V, about USD 233 million for Round VIII, USD 300-400 million expected for Rounds VI and VII, USD 2.35 billion cumulative after four rounds) but no source opened here gives a per-block figure, so workProgramme is null on all 172 block records.
Block-level area is missing for OALP Rounds V and IX (39 blocks). DGH's awardee lists for those rounds carry block, basin and category but no area; only round totals are published.

Basin names are missing at block level for Round I (DGH and PIB give state or offshore area, not basin) and for Round IX in the parsed extract. Terrain (onland / shallow water / deepwater / ultra-deepwater) is DERIVED for every block from the DGH block-code suffix rather than read from a per-block field, and is cross-checked against PIB descriptions only where those exist.

The award dates recorded for OALP Rounds VI (2022-05-06) and OALP Round-V's bid close (2020-06-30) come from trade reporting that was NOT opened for this file. The DGH awardee list for Round VI carries no signing date in its header, unlike the Round VII and Round IX lists. Treat those two dates as unverified.

The four DGH bid tables and five DGH awardee lists were read through the Internet Archive, not from dghindia.gov.in directly. DGH has rebuilt its website and the old /assets/downloads/ paths now return the single-page-application shell for every request, including for files the archive shows were served from those exact URLs. These are archived copies of primary documents, which is stronger than a mirror but weaker than the live record.

CAG Report No. 19 of 2011 is a scanned image with no text layer and no OCR tool was available in this environment. Chapter 4 was read as page images - the chapter opening, the relinquishment finding and the two closing pages on audit access. The remaining chapters were downloaded but not read. A quantified loss estimate elsewhere in the report cannot be ruled out on this basis.

The Public Accounts Committee's 47th Report (16th Lok Sabha) on Hydrocarbon Production Sharing Contracts, which would carry the ministry's formal replies to the CAG findings and the Committee's own conclusions, timed out on repeated download attempts from eparlib.sansad.in and was not read.

No copy of the 24 July 2018 arbitral award, the 9 May 2023 single-judge order or the 14 February 2025 Division Bench judgment was obtained. The KG-D6 litigation records rest on a legal publisher's reports plus press coverage of the Supreme Court hearings. The neutral citation 2025 SCC OnLine Del 841 is recorded so the judgment can be pulled and this file corrected.
The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas demand notices - US$ 1.55 billion (2016) and US$ 2.81 billion (2025) - were not obtained. Both are carried at 'reported' tier from press accounts.

No Reliance Industries statement of its own on the KG-D6 migrated-gas dispute was obtained - no exchange filing, no press release, no annual-report note. The company's position in this file is its counsel's submission in open court as reported by one newspaper. That is thinner than the allegation side of the record and is flagged as such.
mopng.gov.in reset the connection on every attempt from this environment, so the ministry's own DSF and OALP programme pages were never read. Everything on DSF here comes from two PIB releases.

DSF Round-III and Round-IV outcomes are not in this file. DSF-III was launched on 10 June 2021 offering 32 contract areas with 75 discoveries and DSF-IV was launched on 15 April 2025 with 9 contract areas and 55 discoveries; the number of bids received and contracts signed for either is not in any source opened here. The cumulative figure of 85 revenue sharing contracts covering 175 fields across DSF I, II and III is documented from PIB.

The 1997 Cabinet decision approving NELP, the 14 October 2015 DSF policy notification, the March 2016 HELP gazette notification and the February 2019 reform notification were none of them retrieved. All four regime changes are dated from PIB releases and DGH publications rather than from the instruments themselves.
